subject: Private deployment: tenant IO bucketization & node-grid sizing proposal
messages:
From: Rajesh Menon <rajesh@harbortech.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: HarborTech Cloud Ops <cloudops@harbortech.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private Redwood on-prem kick-off: cluster sizing, IO segmentation, and security constraints

Stephanie —

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. We're moving ahead with a private (on-prem) deployment of Redwood in our SaltLake DC and want to lock down the high-level cluster requirements before the preflight. Key constraints and asks from our side:

- 3 clusters (prod, stage, dev) with strict tenancy (prod must be isolated VLAN/subnet).
- Models artifacts + checkpoints (~1.6 PB cold archive, 70 TB hot NVMe for active models).
- Inference node pools: CPU pool for control plane, GPU pool (8 x A100-equivalent) for prod, and burst pool for spot-like capacity.
- Compliance: at-rest encryption with customer-managed KMS, audit logs retention 3 years, and egress to only specific cloud destinations.
- Network: limited MTU (1500), BGP routing to our spine switches, and mandatory IPS/IDS inspection for north-south traffic.

Attached is our current network diagram and a short inventory.

Can you share an opinionated node-grid and storage bucketization proposal (how we should segment PVs, recommended storage classes, eviction thresholds, and backup cadence) ahead of the call? Also please confirm whether Redwood's private control plane can integrate with our KMS and existing SIEM.

Thanks,
Rajesh
VP Infrastructure, HarborTech

--
Attachment: harbortech_network_diagram.pdf (diagram, 2 pages)
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rajesh Menon <rajesh@harbortech.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jan 2028 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private Redwood on-prem kick-off: cluster sizing, IO segmentation, and security constraints

Rajesh —

Thanks, this is very helpful. We can absolutely support customer-managed KMS (integrations via KMIP or cloud KMS proxies) and send audit events to a SIEM over TLS. I've sketched a compact, opinionated plan below to review on the call:

High-level recommendation (summary):
- Three clusters as requested. Prod: 3 control-plane VMs (HA), 6 GPU worker nodes for steady-state inference, plus a 2-node burst pool for additional throughput. Stage: 3 GPU nodes. Dev: 2 CPU-only nodes.
- Storage split into 3 tiers:
  1) Hot NVMe (FastPV): local NVMe on GPU nodes for weights/kv-cache (70 TB aggregate, use LVM + local-ssd CSI for fastest I/O).
  2) Warm blockstore (BlockPV): network-attached SSD-backed blockstore (Ceph/RBD or Blockstore appliances) for snapshots and model checkpoints (200 TB).
  3) Cold archive (Object): S3-compatible object storage for >1PB with lifecycle policies to tape/archive.
- PV strategy: use StorageClass 'fast-local-ssd' for ephemeral caches with reclaimPolicy: Delete, 'durable-block' for persistent checkpoints (reclaimPolicy: Retain), and an 's3-archive' gateway for model archive.
- Kube settings: kubelet evictionThresholds at memory.available=200Mi, nodefs.available=10%, use pod-level local-pv tolerations/taints for inference pods to land on GPU nodes only.
- Networking: Calico in policy-only mode; enforce egress through a NAT gateway per cluster with IP allowlists. MTU 1500 is fine.

I'm looping in Dev and Lauren for the detailed sizing and encryption notes. Can we schedule a 60-minute preflight on Monday?

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

--

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Rajesh Menon <rajesh@harbortech.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Jan 2028 08:26:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private Redwood on-prem kick-off: cluster sizing, IO segmentation, and security constraints

Folks —

Following up with concrete node-grid and storage decisions that map to Redwood runtime behavior. Notes below are pragmatic and tuned for predictable latency and cost.

1) Node grid (prod cluster)
- GPU worker pools:
  - gpustd-8: 6 nodes, each with 8x A100-equivalent, local NVMe for KV cache; allocate 256 GiB host memory and 2TB local NVMe per node. Reserve 10% headroom for OS and kubelet.
  - gpu-burst-8: 2 nodes (same HW) configured as lower-priority with taint: gpu-burst=true:NoSchedule and tolerated only by burst daemonset. Autoscaling is manual for on-prem; we'll include a runbook for cordon/drain and QoS demotion.
- Control plane: 3 x m8.large-equivalent VMs with etcd backed by multi-AZ blockstore. Keep etcd on dedicated disks with iops guarantees.
- CPU pools: 3 x cpu-std nodes for system workloads, monitoring, and sidecars.

2) Storage mapping
- FastPV local-ssd: use local persistent volumes via a LocalPV provisioner for KV caches and temp model shards. These are ephemeral; ensure warm checkpoint replication to durable-block.
- Durable-block: RBD/Ceph or dedicated SAN with QoS across tenants. Provide RPO 1 hour for prod checkpoint replication using async mirroring. Use LVM on top for resize operations.
- Object gateway: MinIO or S3-compatible appliance with lifecycle rules (30d warm -> 90d cold -> archive). Ensure multipart upload tuned for 128 MiB parts for large model artifacts.

3) Backups and retention
- Checkpoints: nightly snapshot + incremental hourly sync to durable-block; weekly full to object archive.
- Audit logs: forward to SIEM with guaranteed 3-year retention (we will hand off rotation configuration).

4) Encryption & KMS
- KMS proxy in customer network, Redwood control plane stores only wrapped keys. At-rest encryption for block devices via dm-crypt; object layer uses server-side encryption with customer-managed KMS.

5) Eviction and QoS
- Pod priority classes: inference-high, inference-batch, infra. Set evictionHard: memory.available<150Mi for inference-high and nodefs.available<8% for all nodes.

Open questions for call:
- Do you have a preferred blockstore vendor (Ceph/NetApp/Pure)? Performance goals (p99 tail) for 1-request model loads?
- Do you require air-gapped delivery of control plane images?

I'll draft a short runbook for node drains and burst activation before the meeting.

- Dev
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: Sat, 20 Jan 2028 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private Redwood on-prem kick-off: cluster sizing, IO segmentation, and security constraints

Thanks all — this looks good and aligns with our internal expectations. A few quick replies:

- Blockstore: currently evaluating Pure and NetApp; Pure preferred for predictable latency but still vetting.
- Performance target: p99 model load < 120ms for hot weights; if local NVMe helps achieve that we are comfortable with replication to durable-block as a second line of defense.
- Air-gap: yes for prod control-plane images — we'll need an image import process and signed manifests.

Available Monday 2028-01-22 10:00-12:00 PST for the 60-min preflight. Please send calendar invite and an agenda.

Rajesh
VP Infrastructure, HarborTech
